markdown_report:
The next experiment should complete an auditable recent-cutoff comparison before adding architecture. The supplied snapshots already identify a `recent10` treatment; they do not establish its improvement over a matched uniform control.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, recent10 changes nonterminal probabilities only for histories longer than twelve events. These represent approximately 16–28% of eligible users across categories, limiting intervention coverage. Second, Industrial and Electronics retain weak-margin rates of 10.93% and 10.25%. These training probes motivate discrimination checks but do not establish held-out ranking quality. Third, snapshots record equal branch counts while definitions describe Bernoulli(0.75) allocation. This conflict prevents reliable attribution until definitions match executed training.

Three literature insights narrow the alternatives. BERT4Rec [1] already uses masked reconstruction and appended-mask inference. Terminal supervision therefore offers task alignment with limited novelty. Sequential Masked Modeling [2] motivates examining window and masking choices. Its reported results do not establish this cutoff policy’s benefit. TiSASRec [3] demonstrates temporal relation modeling. Transferring temporal attention into bidirectional BERT4Rec would require a separate architecture experiment.

The framework separates three directions: **target exposure** through cutoff sampling, **temporal relevance** through attention, and **semantic specificity** through jointly trained text features. Sampling preserves inference; temporal and semantic changes require consistent model and predictor updates. These interventions should be evaluated separately.

Scores below use O/F/U/M/D: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Idea | O/F/U/M/D | Positive reason; negative reason |
|---|---|---|
| Complete audited cutoff comparison [1,2] | 2/6/7/6/3 | Precisely tests recent target exposure; limited novelty and coverage |
| Learned elapsed-time attention [3] | 4/7/7/5/6 | Could distinguish stale interests; purchase gaps do not reveal current intent |
| Joint title/description encoder, inspired by supplied ITS-Rec summary | 4/7/6/5/7 | Could sharpen descriptive matches; text similarity cannot establish compatibility |

At 40% progress, select the **audited cutoff comparison**. It explicitly targets older interests competing with recent preferences and broad associations displacing specific present choices. Strict-prefix prediction may improve context-specific discrimination in Industrial and Electronics, addressing their measured weak-margin tail. These are hypotheses; it cannot identify satisfied needs or unavailable compatibility facts.

Verify the supplied uniform control’s objective, RNG streams and checkpoint rule. Compare it with recent10 while changing only conditional nonterminal probabilities: endpoint probability stays 0.1; remaining mass mixes uniform eligible positions equally with the latest ten. Preserve separately normalized half-weight reconstruction/terminal losses and strict-prefix MASK inputs.

Use one independent BERT4Rec/checkpoint per category, unchanged host macro validation HR@10, and consistent appended-mask prediction. Persist actual branch counts, target exposure, context lengths and checkpoint counters; repair contradictory definitions. Revisit the same twenty users for staleness and specific-choice rationales. The reported 0.5850 and treatment snapshots alone establish neither a controlled gain nor full-catalog improvement.

Resolve epochs as min(200, int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))). All executed training and diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

The supplied snapshots specify 64 independently sampled eligible users per branch, latest-maxlen reconstruction with 0.15 MASK-only corruption and one-target fallback, and terminal contexts of at most maxlen-1 preceding events. Preserve these choices. Use L=0.5*CE_reconstruction_sum/N_reconstruction+0.5*CE_terminal_sum/N_terminal, with both counts positive. Preserve the supplied real-item-only full-softmax denominator, tied item embeddings, ID-minus-one labels and no output bias. Do not add negative mining, change endpoint probability, replace equal branch counts with Bernoulli allocation or change the loss denominator in this experiment.

For histories of length n>2, the terminal endpoint has probability 0.1. Conditional nonterminal control probabilities are uniform over zero-based positions 1..n-2. Treatment probabilities mix that uniform distribution equally with uniform selection from its latest min(10,n-2) positions. Histories shorter than two events are ineligible; length-two histories select their only eligible endpoint. The arms coincide for n<=12. The 0.1 endpoint probability refers only to terminal-branch selection; reconstruction can additionally supervise the endpoint.

Retain the supplied SeedSequence([42, category_id, one_based_epoch, zero_based_batch, purpose_id]) streams, purpose IDs users=0, cutoffs=1, masks=2, negatives=3, and reconstruction-then-terminal user draw order. Match streams and cutoff uniforms across arms where the host permits; keep model/dropout RNG separate. Do not claim hardware-level determinism.

Terminal inputs include only occurrences before the selected target followed by reserved MASK. Exclude the selected occurrence and all subsequent occurrences, retaining earlier repetitions. Reconstruction uses genuine masked labels without shifted-target leakage. All histories remain left padded; use the maximum nonpadding index for readout. Inference appends MASK with identical truncation, and the embedded predictor writer must preserve this architecture and category routing.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats and predict_score interfaces. Correct branch-allocation definitions to describe measured equal-count training, and persist selected-checkpoint counters explicitly. Report branch examples, targets, CE sums, denominators, coefficient masses, endpoint exceptions, long-history exposure, target frequencies, context lengths and timing. Unmatched probe bookkeeping remains unavailable; do not reconstruct branch allocation from final-position coverage. RankMe concentration is not proof of collapse.

Select using unchanged host macro validation HR@10. The snapshot category scores average to 0.58125, whereas inspirations report 0.5850; these must not be treated as one verified evaluation. Record their provenance separately. If aligned host per-user outcomes are available, report gained/lost hits and a paired within-category bootstrap; otherwise omit uncertainty estimates. Use the same twenty real training users for full-catalog unseen-item qualitative follow-up, tracking staleness and concrete recent-choice rationales separately from duplicate-capability or compatibility rejections. Only histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available; infer neither unavailable attributes nor current needs as facts.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')

def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))

def choose_target(history, u, treatment=True):
    """Zero-based occurrence index; u is one matched uniform draw."""
    n = len(history)
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Terminal histories require preceding context')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    m = n - 2
    probabilities = np.full(m, 1.0 / m)
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = np.cumsum(probabilities)
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    t = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1) + 1
    return t, 'nonterminal'

def terminal_example(history, u, maxlen, mask_id, treatment=True):
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError('maxlen must allow context and MASK')
    t, status = choose_target(history, u, treatment)
    context = list(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t])
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    tokens = context + [mask_id]
    sequence[-len(tokens):] = tokens
    return sequence, int(history[t]), status

originality.positive: Fixed endpoint exposure and a precisely isolated nonterminal sampling change produce an interpretable BERT4Rec adaptation.
originality.negative: Masked terminal prediction and recency sampling have established precedents; the contribution is experimental control rather than a new backbone.

future_potential.positive: A verified comparison can establish whether target exposure merits further temporal or semantic modeling while addressing stale-interest and broad-association failures.
future_potential.negative: Only approximately 16–28% of eligible histories receive different cutoff probabilities, and effects conflate target exposure with context length. Compatibility and satisfied needs remain unobserved.

code_difficulty.positive: The sampler changes without changing BERT4Rec architecture or inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable attribution requires matched control configuration, RNG handling, checkpoint-specific counters and corrected diagnostic definitions.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item modeling and appended-mask next-item inference.
Provides the required backbone and a precedent for terminal prediction.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff policy's performance on the pinned benchmark.
Limits novelty claims for terminal masking itself.

related_work.title: Sequential Masked Modeling
contributions: The supplied search summary reports investigation of sliding windows and penultimate-token masking.
Motivates examining supervision alignment before adding architectural complexity.
limitations: Its reported findings do not verify the proposed nonterminal cutoff mixture under the fixed RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models absolute positions and pairwise elapsed-time relations.
Provides a temporal-attention precedent for a later separate BERT4Rec adaptation.
limitations: Its backbone must not replace the required BERT4Rec family.
Purchase intervals do not directly reveal engagement, compatibility or unsatisfied current needs.

related_work.title: ITS-Rec (2025), as summarized in the supplied search results
contributions: The supplied summary describes incorporating textual item representations into sequential recommendation.
Motivates a future jointly trained title/description encoder within one model.
limitations: The supplied summary attributes substantial gains to reviews, which are unavailable here.
Does not establish the proposed from-scratch, titles-and-descriptions-only BERT4Rec variant.
